comments.bodyHTML:
@fgallegosalido any thoughts about this issue, why this fails with ConnextDDS?

  • where CFT is set,

rclcpp/rclcpp/src/rclcpp/parameter_event_handler.cpp

Lines 77 to 107 in 6ff4d83

bool
ParameterEventHandler::configure_nodes_filter(const std::vector<std::string> & node_names)
{
if (node_names.empty()) {
// Clear content filter
event_subscription_->set_content_filter("");
if (event_subscription_->is_cft_enabled()) {
return false;
}
return true;
}
std::string filter_expression;
size_t total = node_names.size();
for (size_t i = 0; i < total; ++i) {
filter_expression += "node = %" + std::to_string(i);
if (i < total - 1) {
filter_expression += " OR ";
}
}
// Enclose each node name in "'".
std::vector<std::string> quoted_node_names;
for (const auto & name : node_names) {
quoted_node_names.push_back("'" + resolve_path(name) + "'");
}
event_subscription_->set_content_filter(filter_expression, quoted_node_names);
return event_subscription_->is_cft_enabled();
}

  • where the test fails,

rclcpp/rclcpp/test/rclcpp/test_parameter_event_handler.cpp

Line 515 in 6ff4d83

EXPECT_EQ(received_from_remote_node1, false);

I’ve found that ConnextDDS has some kind of invocation limitation. I’m currently unable to explain the reason for this.
Below is a sample code. When using the code in (1), the configured content filter does not work. Only when using the method in (2) does the content filter take effect. FastDDS does not have this limitation.

int main(int argc, char * argv[])
{
  rclcpp::init(argc, argv);

  rclcpp::NodeOptions options;
  options.enable_rosout(false);
  auto node = std::make_shared<rclcpp::Node>("test_parameter_event_handler");

  std::string remote_node1_name = "remote_node1";
  auto remote_node1 = std::make_shared<rclcpp::Node>(remote_node1_name, options);
  std::string remote_node2_name = "remote_node2";
  auto remote_node2 = std::make_shared<rclcpp::Node>(remote_node2_name, options);

  auto param_handler = std::make_shared<rclcpp::ParameterEventHandler>(node); // (1)

  const std::string remote_node1_param_name = "param_remote_node1";
  const std::string remote_node2_param_name = "param_remote_node2";
  remote_node1->declare_parameter(remote_node1_param_name, 10);
  remote_node2->declare_parameter(remote_node2_param_name, "Default");

  //auto param_handler = std::make_shared<rclcpp::ParameterEventHandler>(node); // (2)

  std::atomic_bool received_from_remote_node1{false};
  std::atomic_bool received_from_remote_node2{false};
  auto cb =
    [&node, &received_from_remote_node1, &received_from_remote_node2, &remote_node1_name, &remote_node2_name]
    (const rcl_interfaces::msg::ParameterEvent & event) {
      //RCLCPP_INFO(node->get_logger(), "Received parameter event from node: %s", event.node.c_str());
      if (event.node == "/" + remote_node1_name) {
        received_from_remote_node1 = true;
      } else if (event.node == "/" + remote_node2_name) {
        received_from_remote_node2 = true;
      }
    };
  auto handler = param_handler->add_parameter_event_callback(cb);

  rclcpp::executors::SingleThreadedExecutor executor;
  executor.add_node(node);
  executor.add_node(remote_node1);
  executor.add_node(remote_node2);

  auto wait_param_event = [&executor]
    (std::chrono::seconds timeout) {
      auto start = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
      while (std::chrono::steady_clock::now() - start < timeout) {
        executor.spin_some();
        std::this_thread::sleep_for(100ms);
      }
    };

  RCLCPP_INFO(node->get_logger(), "Configuring parameter event handler to filter out events from remote_node2");
  if (!param_handler->configure_nodes_filter({"remote_node2"})) {
    RCLCPP_ERROR(node->get_logger(), "Failed to configure nodes filter");
    rclcpp::shutdown();
    return 1;
  }

  {
    std::thread thread(wait_param_event, 1s);
    std::this_thread::sleep_for(100ms);
    remote_node1->set_parameter(rclcpp::Parameter(remote_node1_param_name, 30));
    remote_node2->set_parameter(rclcpp::Parameter(remote_node2_param_name, "def"));
    thread.join();
    if (received_from_remote_node1) {
      RCLCPP_INFO(node->get_logger(), "Received parameter event from %s", remote_node1_name.c_str());
    }
    if (received_from_remote_node2) {
      RCLCPP_INFO(node->get_logger(), "Received parameter event from %s", remote_node2_name.c_str());
    }
  }

  rclcpp::shutdown();
  return 0;
}

comments.body:
i investigated the root cause and i believe this is a test issue, not a ConnextDDS bug.
ConnextDDS is actually honoring the message delivery sequence correctly here.

the key finding: when ParameterEventHandler is created before declare_parameter, the subscription to /parameter_events already exists without a content filter when declare_parameter is called. since declare_parameter internally triggers parameter events, those events are delivered to the unfiltered subscription and queued in the subscriber's cache. when configure_nodes_filter is called later, it only applies to future incoming messages — the already-queued events remain in the cache.
the /parameter_events topic uses rmw_qos_profile_parameter_events(keep last, depth 1000), so the subscription holds onto those previously received messages as expected. once data is in the reader's cache, it has been validly received and should not be retroactively purged when the filter changes. FastDDS likely re-evaluates already-queued samples against the updated filter or has different timing, which is why the test passes there — but that behavior is arguably less correct?
when ParameterEventHandler is created after declare_parameter, the content filter works correctly with ConnextDDS because no stale events exist in the queue.

after all, the test should be updated to either create ParameterEventHandler after declare_parameter, or drain/ignore pre-existing events before asserting filter behavior.
